text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- The small number of people attending a rally held by the conservative coalition partner -- the True Path Party -- over the weekend shows how the party has melted since it went into a coalition with the Islamists.
- Turkey's railway chief says the rail system in Turkey cannot make a profit for at least 10 years even if money was invested in the sector and ticket prices pushed up.
HURRIYET

- Slogans supporting the strict Islamic Sharia law were chanted by crowds at a rally protesting at an education plan sponsored by the secularist army that would effectively shut down the middle sections of state religious schools.
- True Path Party Tansu Ciller cannot decide on who to appoint to the recently-vacated trade and industry and health ministries from among the hundreds of eager candidates in her party.
MILLIYET
- A study reveals that electricity prices in Turkey are the highest and consumption is lowest among member countries of the Organisation for Cooperation in Economy and Development (OECD).

- The United States Congress research deparment said in its report that Turkey's Islamist-led government will coopearate with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) despite Islamist opposition to such Western institutions during its election campaign.
YENI YUZYIL

- A senior military commander says that the Islamist-led government will either have to go or knuckle under and implement plans demanded by the powerful secularist army as measures to curb Islamist activism.
- A banned type of coal which has radioactive properties is being used at thermal power plants in the coastal holiday resort region of Mugla.
RADIKAL
- Turkey has one week left to implement regulations to fight money laundering before it is declared a "black money" haven.
CUMHURIYET
- The Turkish army kills 26 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerillas in operations held on its border with Iraq.
- Women organisations call for democracy on "mother's day".
DUNYA
- The Turkish food sector is determined to fight against quota and duty concessions given to the European Union (EU) under a customs union deal which went into effect last year.

- A business organisation in Western Turkey calls for factory shut-down protests to demonstrate against the present political and economic unease created as politicians squabble with each other and the powerful army.
ZAMAN
- The Turkish armed forces has launched its final cross-border operation against Kurdish rebels in northern Iraq.
